bull.b: Sustained higher gross and net margins provide durable earnings power and insulating operating leverage. Strong margins give management flexibility to fund live-ops, marketing, and development without eroding profitability, supporting long-term cash generation and reinvestment priorities.

Repeated free-cash-flow generation, including a 2025 rebound, signals the company can self-fund operations and selective user acquisition. Durable cash conversion reduces reliance on external financing and underpins capacity for live-service investment and balance-sheet resilience over months.

Minimal leverage lowers bankruptcy and interest-rate risk and preserves strategic optionality. Low debt affords management time to address user and revenue softness, pursue product or market pivots, and avoid near-term refinancing pressures that could impair long-term execution.

bear.t: Multi-year revenue declines and weakening KPIs
bear.b: Repeated revenue declines and deteriorating bookings/paying-user metrics indicate structural demand challenges. Even with higher monetization per payer, a shrinking payer base undermines sustainable top-line growth and makes upside dependent on reversing user trends rather than margin moves alone.

Negative equity constrains capital-raising options and can restrict strategic moves (M&A, buybacks, or equity financing). Over time this structural balance-sheet weakness reduces resilience to shocks and may raise stakeholder scrutiny or limit long-term investment flexibility.

bear.t: Concentration on a single live-service title
bear.b: Heavy reliance on one flagship live-service game creates product-concentration risk: declines in engagement or paying users materially affect revenue. This dependence limits diversification benefits and makes structural growth sensitive to one title's lifecycle and content cadence.
